spex.caption: The editio princeps: Exercitia spiritualia, Rome 1548 — the Vulgata's title page with the IHS device, the year Paul III approved the book.
spex.credit: Exercitia spiritualia (Rome: Antonio Blado, 1548). Internet Archive bub_gb_eyZ68wmgWoIC, leaf 8. Public domain.

fabri.caption: Title page of the editio princeps of the Memoriale, Paris 1873 — the printing this edition is made from.
fabri.credit: Memoriale Beati Petri Fabri, ed. Marcel Bouix, S.J. (Paris: Albanel, 1873). Internet Archive memorialebeatipe0000sign, leaf 9. Public domain.

ratio.caption: The Ratio's engraved title in the Roman printing of 1606 — Ignatius above the rulebook of the schools.
ratio.credit: Ratio atque institutio studiorum Societatis Iesu (Rome: in Collegio Romano, 1606; the definitive text of 1599). Internet Archive bub_gb_6mcuvbXlgXEC, leaf 0. Public domain. The module's text follows the Florence printing of 1893.

conimbricenses.caption: Title page of the 1617 printing of the Coimbra De anima commentary — the very printing this edition was transcribed from.
conimbricenses.credit: Commentarii Collegii Conimbricensis, in tres libros De anima (1617). Internet Archive commentariicolle00col, leaf 5. Public domain.

rodriguez.caption: Title page of the Dublin printing of 1861 — the anonymous English this edition carries.
rodriguez.credit: Rodríguez, The Practice of Christian and Religious Perfection, vol. I (Dublin: James Duffy, 1861). Internet Archive PracticeOfChristianAndReligiousPerfectionV1, leaf 5. Public domain.

caussade.caption: Title page of McMahon's English of 1887 — Ramière's arrangement, as this edition carries it.
caussade.credit: Abandonment; or, Absolute Surrender to Divine Providence (New York: Benziger, 1887). Internet Archive abandonmentorabs00caus, leaf 5. Public domain.

xavier.caption: Title page of Coleridge's Life and Letters, vol. I — the biography that carries the letters complete.
xavier.credit: H. J. Coleridge, S.J., The Life and Letters of St. Francis Xavier, vol. I (London: Burns and Oates; first published 1872). Internet Archive lifelettersofstf01cole, leaf 7. Public domain.

acosta.caption: Title page of the Hakluyt Society printing of Grimston's 1604 English — the text this edition carries.
acosta.credit: Acosta, The Natural and Moral History of the Indies, ed. Markham (London: Hakluyt Society, 1880). Internet Archive naturalmoralhist01acos, leaf 11. Public domain.

relations.caption: Title page of Thwaites's vol. XXXIV — Lower Canada and the Hurons, 1649: the volume of St-Ignace and the martyrdoms this edition selects from.
relations.credit: The Jesuit Relations and Allied Documents, vol. XXXIV (Cleveland: Burrows, 1898). Internet Archive jesuits34jesuuoft, leaf 9. Public domain.

spee_cautio.caption: Title page of the first printing, Rinteln 1631 — the book published without Spee's name, transcribed here by eye from this copy.
spee_cautio.credit: Cautio Criminalis, seu de processibus contra sagas liber (Rinteln: Petrus Lucius, 1631). Internet Archive per_witchcraft-...-1631_911, leaf 0. Public domain.

monita.caption: The hostile edition wears its colours: the frontispiece “A Jesuit” of Brownlee's New York printing of 1857 — the forgery's polemical afterlife, made visible in the very edition whose facing texts this module carries.
monita.credit: Secreta Monita Societatis Jesu / The Secret Instructions of the Jesuits, ed. W. C. Brownlee (New York, 1857), frontispiece. Internet Archive instructiosecret00browrich, leaf 7. Public domain.

dominus.caption: Title page of the Lisbon printing of 1773, Latin and Portuguese — the brief of suppression as it reached the kingdoms.
dominus.credit: Breve do Santissimo Padre Clemente XIV (Lisbon, 1773). Internet Archive sanctissimidomin00cath_5, leaf 1. Public domain.

imago.caption: The engraved title of the Imago primi saeculi, Antwerp 1640 — the Society's self-portrait at its centenary.
imago.credit: Imago primi saeculi Societatis Iesu (Antwerp: Plantin press of Balthasar Moretus, 1640). Internet Archive imagoprimisaecul00boll; the same image opens the module's reader. Public domain.

spee_trutz.caption: A page of “Bey stiller Nacht” in the Cologne printing of 1654 — the facsimile the module's reader carries beside the transcription.
spee_trutz.credit: Trutznachtigall (Cologne, 1654). Internet Archive trutz-nachtigall-oder-geistlichs-poetisc; the same image appears in the module's reader. Public domain.

paraguay.caption: The witness who was no Jesuit: the title page of the London printing of 1759 — Muratori's Relation 'wrote originally in Italian … and now done into English from the French translation' — with the contemporary owner's inscription of one Mary Ann Beresford across its head.
paraguay.credit: L. A. Muratori, A Relation of the Missions of Paraguay (London: J. Marmaduke, 1759), title page. Internet Archive bim_eighteenth-century_a-relation-of-the-missio_muratori-lodovico-anton_1759, leaf 0, verified against the image. Public domain.
